display.title: With Joy and From the Heart: Why One Mitzvah Is Worth More Than Gan Eden
display.summary_short: Before Shavuos, the storyteller explains why one mitzvah in this world is worth more than all of Olam Haba, with stories of the Rambam and of Reb Hillel of Paritch.
display.summary_long: As we prepare for Shavuos, the storyteller explains that listening to the Aseres HaDibros in shul is like standing at Har Sinai. He then takes up the Mishnah in Pirkei Avos: one moment of teshuvah and good deeds in this world is worth more than all of Olam Haba, yet one moment of Olam Haba is sweeter than every pleasure of this world. A story of the Rambam unmasking doctors who faked curing a man born blind shows why we cannot imagine Olam Haba. The answer to the puzzle: a mitzvah joins us to Hashem Himself, like a child who wants Mommy and not her picture, or a boy who would rather bring the Rebbe a sefer than earn a reward. The Alter Rebbe would say, 'I want only You.' Finally, Reb Hillel of Paritch tells Chassidim of Rabbi Meir of Rottenburg, who stayed in prison rather than let the community be drained by ransom, and of the man who later redeemed his body and chose a place beside him in Gan Eden. Reb Hillel's surprising verdict: he should have chosen to live and put on tefillin one more day.
display.lesson: A mitzvah connects us to Hashem Himself, so we should do every mitzvah with joy and from deep inside, especially as we prepare to receive the Torah on Shavuos.
